titleText.es: Las partículas portadoras de fuerza imparable no pueden, por definición, interactuar con materia inamovible.
titleText.en: Unstoppable force-carrying particles can't interact with immovable matter by definition.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish title and title text are preserved exactly from the Spanish archive, while the English fields reproduce official xkcd #3084. OCR read every Spanish word but interleaved the two top labels; this artifact restores their visual left-to-right order and inventories the three large diagram arrows as separate nonlexical symbols.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Imparable describes something that cannot be stopped. Its singular form is the same with masculine and feminine nouns.
Inamovible describes something that cannot be moved or shifted. Its singular form is the same with masculine and feminine nouns.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to; introduces who has the impression
cardDefinitions.noteEn: With parecer, a can introduce or clarify the person or group who gets an impression. A matching me, te, le, nos, os, or les still appears with the verb.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to that person or group; marks who has the impression
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Before parecer, le identifies one person, one thing, or a grammatically singular group that experiences the impression. English may express the same idea with “to” or by making that person the subject of “find.”

example.en: The idea seems useful to her.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Escenario can mean a stage, but it also means an imagined or possible situation being considered.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: fuerza imparable · objeto inamovible · atravesar sin interactuar
cardDefinitions.questionEn: How does the diagram sidestep the classic unstoppable-force paradox?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: The force passes through the object without interacting, so neither one has to stop or move the other.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The familiar paradox asks what happens when something that cannot be stopped meets something that cannot be moved. The drawing preserves both descriptions by showing the arrow-like force continuing through the block. The title text gives the mock-physics rule behind that visual answer: unstoppable force carriers cannot interact with immovable matter.

applications.explanationEn: The two accented words por qué ask for the reason; they are not the one-word answer connector porque.
Por qué introduces the unknown reason inside the larger statement beginning no entiendo, so qué keeps its written accent.
A la gente names the group having the impression, and le repeats that grammatically singular group before parece.
Parece reports an impression, and complicado names the apparent quality.
Complicado uses masculine singular -o because it describes the masculine singular noun escenario; este sits between them but is not part of this adjective target.
